# Pathland DOM renderer / asset serving — full trace

Below is the end-to-end picture: which classes serve what, where the bundle lives, how the SSR emits its URLs, and how the bundle is built/copied. All paths are absolute.

---

## 0. Mental model: the emitted URL surface

The reserved framework prefix is `/_pathland` (`PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE`). Per mounted app the base becomes `/{mount}/_pathland` (`PathlandRegistry.base()`).

| Asset | Root mount URL | Mounted app URL (e.g. `/app2`) | Produced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| DOM renderer JS | `/_pathland/dom-renderer-<sha256-12>.js` | `/app2/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js` | `PathlandSession.renderHtml` + `PathlandAssets` manifest |
| Base design CSS | `/_pathland/base-<sha256-12>.css` | `/app2/_pathland/base-<hash>.css` | `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked` + `BaseCss` |
| Icon glyph | `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` | `/app2/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` | Java/Rust HTML renderer icon table |
| Service worker | `/_pathland/sw.js` | `/app2/_pathland/sw.js` | app static resource / filter |
| Media assets | `/_pathland/assets/**` | typically same absolute path | demo hosts |
| WebSocket | `/_pathland/ws` | `/app2/_pathland/ws` | starter/extension sockets |

The SSR document carries `data-pathland-base="/_pathland"` (or `"/app2/_pathland"`), plus optional `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` and `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"`.

---

# 1. `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/`

## 1.1 `PathlandIndexController` — the SSR and framework-asset controller

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/java/dev/pathland/spring/PathlandIndexController.java`

This is the only Spring class that serves HTML/assets. There is **no `WebMvcConfigurer` and no `addResourceHandlers`** anywhere in the module; it uses explicit `@GetMapping`s.

**Configuration seams** (lines 50–81):

```java
@Controller
public class PathlandIndexController {                       // line 45

    @Value("${pathland.asset-dir:}")
    private String assetDir;                                  // lines 50-53

    @Value("${pathland.seo.enabled:true}") private boolean seoEnabled;
    @Value("${pathland.seo.site-name:}") private String seoSiteName;
    @Value("${pathland.seo.image:}") private String seoImage;
    ...
```

- `pathland.asset-dir` is an optional **filesystem directory** served under `/_pathland/**` (used by the Spring demo to serve extracted media with Range support).
- `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` are real routes (lines 88–104).

**SPA catch-all** (lines 123–141):

```java
@GetMapping(value = "/{*path}", headers = "!Upgrade")
@ResponseBody
public ResponseEntity<String> index(HttpServletRequest request) {
    MountMatch match = host.match(request.getRequestURI());
    if (match == null) return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
    String html = match.registry().renderHtml(
            match.route(), request.getParameter("wid"), pageMetadata(request));
    return ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.TEXT_HTML).body(html);
}
```

`headers = "!Upgrade"` ensures WebSocket handshakes are not swallowed.

**Framework asset handler — the key one** (lines 161–234):

```java
@GetMapping(value = {"/_pathland/**", "/{app}/_pathland/**"}, headers = "!Upgrade")
@ResponseBody
public ResponseEntity<?> framework(HttpServletRequest request) throws IOException {
    String uri = request.getRequestURI();
    int idx = uri.indexOf("/_pathland/");
    if (idx < 0) return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
    String file = uri.substring(idx + "/_pathland/".length());

    if ("sw.js".equals(file)) {
        Resource sw = classpathFrameworkResource(file);
        if (sw == null || !sw.exists()) return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
        try (InputStream in = sw.getInputStream()) {
            return ResponseEntity.ok()
                .contentType(new MediaType("application", "javascript"))
                .header("Service-Worker-Allowed", "/")
                .cacheControl(CacheControl.noCache())
                .body(in.readAllBytes());
        }
    }

    Resource resource = classpathFrameworkResource(file);
    if (resource == null) resource = diskAsset(file);
    if (resource == null || !resource.exists()) {
        ResponseEntity<?> cssResponse = baseCss(file);
        if (cssResponse != null) return cssResponse;
        ResponseEntity<?> icon = iconGlyph(file);
        if (icon != null) return icon;
        return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
    }
    MediaType type = MediaTypeFactory.getMediaType(file)
            .orElse(MediaType.APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM);
    String rangeHeader = request.getHeader(HttpHeaders.RANGE);
    if (rangeHeader != null && !rangeHeader.isEmpty()) {
        return rangeResponse(resource, type, rangeHeader);
    }
    try (InputStream in = resource.getInputStream()) {
        return ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(type)
            .header(HttpHeaders.ACCEPT_RANGES, "bytes")
            .cacheControl(CacheControl.maxAge(Duration.ofDays(7)).cachePublic().immutable())
            .body(in.readAllBytes());
    }
}
```

Resolution order: **classpath → disk → renderer-owned CSS → renderer-owned icons**:

- `classpathFrameworkResource` (lines 281–285):

```java
ClassPathResource resource = new ClassPathResource("static/_pathland/" + file);
return resource.exists() ? resource : null;
```

- `diskAsset` (lines 287–299): reads `${pathland.asset-dir}`, normalizes and guards against traversal.
- `baseCss` (lines 236–255): returns `HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` when `file.equals(HtmlRenderer.baseCssName())`, with `max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- `iconGlyph` (lines 257–279): `icons/<name>.svg` via `HtmlRenderer.iconSvg`, `max-age=30 days, immutable`.
- `rangeResponse` (lines 301–347): full byte-range support, `206 Partial Content`, `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges.

```

    var registration = registry.addHandler(new PathlandSocket(r), r.base() + "/ws");

```

## 1.3 Registration / metadata files

## 1.4 WebSocket path

`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/java/dev/pathland/spring/PathlandSocket.java` lines 35–38:

```java

    this.registry = registry;

```

So root → `/_pathland/ws`, mounted → `/app2/_pathland/ws`.

## 1.5 What the starter jar itself contains

**It does not contain the DOM renderer bundle.** Its `src/main/resources` has only `META-INF/spring.factories` and the auto-config import. The demo/consumer must put the bundle + `dom-renderer.current` under its own `src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`. Spring Boot’s default static handler also maps `classpath:/static/**`, but the explicit `/_pathland/**` controller mapping takes precedence.

Test-only fixture: `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/test/resources/static/_pathland/sw.js` (no JS bundle).

# 2. `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/` + `pathland-quarkus-deployment/`

## 2.1 How Quarkus serves static files

Quarkus serves `META-INF/resources/**` from the application (and dependency jars) **before JAX-RS**, so the global `/_pathland/**` bundle is normally served by Quarkus’s static-resource handler, not by `IndexResource`. The extension only adds explicit JAX-RS routes for things that have no static file (CSS/icons) and for **mounted** app bases (`/{app}/_pathland/**`), because Quarkus’s static handler only serves the global `/_pathland/**` tree.

## 2.2 `IndexResource` — SSR + mounted-base framework files + CSS/icons

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/IndexResource.java`

`@Path("/")` at line 39.

**Root page** (lines 74–80):

```java
@GET
@Produces(MediaType.TEXT_HTML)
public Response index(@QueryParam("wid") String wid, @Context UriInfo uri,
        @Context HttpHeaders headers) {
    return render("/", wid, uri, headers);
}
```

`/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` at lines 82–102.

**Deep-link catch-all with framework-path interception** (lines 104–123):

```java
@GET
@Path("{path:(?!_pathland)(?!q/).*}")
@Produces(MediaType.TEXT_HTML)
public Response deep(@PathParam("path") String path, @QueryParam("wid") String wid,
        @Context UriInfo uri, @Context HttpHeaders headers) throws IOException {
    int framework = path.indexOf("/_pathland/");
    if (framework >= 0) {
        return frameworkFile(path.substring(framework + "/_pathland/".length()));
    }
    return render("/" + path, wid, uri, headers);
}
```

The negative lookahead excludes:
- the **global** `/_pathland/**` (left to Quarkus static resources),
- Quarkus non-application `/q/**`.

But a **mounted** path like `/ad/_pathland/dom-renderer-….js` is caught here and routed to `frameworkFile`.

**Renderer-owned icon and CSS routes** (lines 193–210):

```java
@GET
@Path("/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg")
@Produces("image/svg+xml")
public Response icon(@PathParam("name") String name) { return iconResponse(name); }

@GET
@Path("/_pathland/{name}.css")
@Produces("text/css")
public Response baseCss(@PathParam("name") String name) {
    Response css = baseCssResponse(name + ".css");
    return css != null ? css : Response.status(Response.Status.NOT_FOUND).build();
}
```

**Mounted-app framework file resolution** (lines 212–235):

```java
private Response frameworkFile(String file) throws IOException {
    // Quarkus web static lives in META-INF/resources (classpath resource root), so the
    // shared `/_pathland/**` mount resolves as /META-INF/resources/_pathland/<file>.
    try (InputStream in = getClass().getResourceAsStream(
            "/META-INF/resources/_pathland/" + file)) {
        if (in != null) {
            return Response.ok(in.readAllBytes()).type(mediaTypeOf(file)).build();
        }
    }
    Response css = baseCssResponse(file);
    if (css != null) return css;
    if (file.startsWith("icons/") && file.endsWith(".svg")
            && file.substring("icons/".length(), file.length() - ".svg".length()).indexOf('/') < 0) {
        return iconResponse(file.substring("icons/".length(), file.length() - ".svg".length()));
    }
    return Response.status(Response.Status.NOT_FOUND).build();
}
```

- `baseCssResponse` (lines 237–255) serves the content-hashed CSS with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- `iconResponse` (lines 257–268) serves SVG with `max-age=2592000, immutable`.
- `mediaTypeOf` (lines 270–284) maps `.js`, `.svg`, `.mp3`, `.mp4`, else octet-stream.

Note: `frameworkFile` has **no Range handling** and **no filesystem asset-dir seam**; it reads classpath bytes.

## 2.3 `ServiceWorkerFilter`

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/ServiceWorkerFilter.java`

Quarkus’s static handler doesn’t send `Service-Worker-Allowed` / `no-cache`, so this filter intercepts `/_pathland/sw.js` (and mounted bases) before routes.

Lines 42–69:

```java
private static final String RESOURCE = "META-INF/resources/_pathland/sw.js";
private static final String PATH_SUFFIX = "/_pathland/sw.js";

void init(@Observes Filters filters) {
    filters.register(context -> {
        if (!context.normalizedPath().endsWith(PATH_SUFFIX)) { context.next(); return; }
        byte[] script = readResource();
        if (script == null) { context.next(); return; } // fail open
        context.response()
            .putHeader("Content-Type", "text/javascript;charset=UTF-8")
            .putHeader("Service-Worker-Allowed", "/")
            .putHeader("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
            .end(Buffer.buffer(script));
    }, 100);
}
```

Classloading fallback (lines 72–102): thread-context loader → this class’s loader → system loader. This is needed because the extension runtime loader may not see the application’s `META-INF/resources` copy.

# 3. `lib/java/pathland-server-core/` — SSR and emitted URLs

## 3.1 Framework base resolution

`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandSession.java` lines 57–60:

```java
/** The reserved framework path prefix (spec): host system endpoints ... live under
 *  {@code /_pathland/**} ... */
public static final String PATHLAND_BASE = "/_pathland";
```

`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandRegistry.java` lines 142–145:

public String base() {
    return "/".equals(mountPath)
            ? PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE

So `/` → `/_pathland`, `/app2` → `/app2/_pathland`.

`PathlandHost.match` (lines 100–111) chooses the longest mount and returns the mount-stripped route; `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml` (lines 197–222) creates a throwaway `PathlandSession` with that `base()` and renders.

## 3.2 The actual SSR HTML construction

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandSession.java` lines 444–475:

```java
public String renderHtml(boolean serviceWorker, boolean ssrScoped, PageMetadata pageMetadata) {
    HtmlRenderer renderer = HtmlRenderer.tryInstance();
    if (renderer == null) {
        return "<!DOCTYPE html>... Pathland renderer unavailable ...";
    }
    ProtocolFrame frame = ssrFrame();
    DocumentMeta meta = documentMeta(pageMetadata);
    String html = debugHtml
            ? renderer.renderLinkedDebug(frame, rootId, base, meta)
            : renderer.renderLinked(frame, rootId, base, meta);

    String htmlAttrs = " data-pathland-base=\"" + base + "\""
            + (serviceWorker ? " data-pathland-service-worker=\"true\"" : "")
            + (ssrScoped ? " data-pathland-ssr-scoped=\"true\"" : "");
    String integrity = PathlandAssets.bundleIntegrity();
    String integrityAttr = integrity.isEmpty() ? "" : " integrity=\"" + integrity + "\"";
    return injectHtmlAttributes(html, htmlAttrs)
            .replace("</body>", "<script src=\"" + base + "/" + PathlandAssets.bundleName()
                    + "\"" + integrityAttr + " defer></script></body>");
}
```

Key facts:
- **The script tag is injected by `PathlandSession`** just before `</body>`.
- **`data-pathland-base` is injected on the `<html>` tag** by `injectHtmlAttributes` (lines 503–518).
- The CSS link is emitted by the renderer, not by `PathlandSession` (see below).
- If `HtmlRenderer` is unavailable, an “unavailable” document is returned with no script.

## 3.3 CSS `<link>` emission

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/HtmlRenderer.java`

```java
private static String linkedCssHead(String cssBase) {
    String base = cssBase;
    while (base.endsWith("/")) base = base.substring(0, base.length() - 1);
    return "<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"" + Format.escapeHtmlAttr(base) + "/"
            + BaseCss.builtinCssName() + "\">";
}
```

`renderLinked` falls back to inline CSS if either the base or the CSS name is empty (lines 106–108).

`BaseCss` (`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/BaseCss.java` lines 12–25) reads the classpath resources `/dev/pathland/render/html/base.css` and `base.css.name`.

Icons: `HtmlRenderer.iconSvg(name)` lines 158–168 renders `/<svg>` from the `Icons` table.

## 3.4 `PathlandAssets` — content-hashed bundle manifest

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandAssets.java`

Manifest lookup paths (lines 38–45):

```java
static final String MANIFEST = "dom-renderer.current";
static final String FALLBACK = "dom-renderer.js";

private static final String[] MANIFEST_PATHS = {
    "META-INF/resources/_pathland/" + MANIFEST,  // Quarkus demo
    "static/_pathland/" + MANIFEST,               // Spring Boot demo
    "_pathland/" + MANIFEST,                      // generic
};
```

Resolution semantics (lines 110–127):

```java
static Manifest resolveManifest(Lookup lookup) {
    for (String path : MANIFEST_PATHS) {
        try (InputStream in = lookup.open(path)) {
            ...
            List<String> lines = readLines(in, 2);
            String name = lines.isEmpty() ? "" : lines.get(0).trim();
            if (validBundleName(name)) {
                String integrity = lines.size() > 1 ? lines.get(1).trim() : "";
                return new Manifest(name, validIntegrity(integrity) ? integrity : "");
            }
        } catch (IOException ignored) {}
    }
    return new Manifest(FALLBACK, "");
}
```

- The first line is the content-hashed filename.
- The second line is an optional `sha384-<base64>` SRI digest.
- Fallback is the pre-hash literal `dom-renderer.js` with no integrity.
- Resolution is classloader-aware (thread context first, then own loader, then system — lines 71–102, 129–142), cached per loader.
- `bundleName()` / `bundleIntegrity()` at lines 61–69 are the only public-ish seams used by `PathlandSession`.

## 3.5 What server-core does *not* serve

`pathland-server-core` contains **no HTTP server / asset handler**. It only emits URLs and resolves the bundle name. Serving is the host framework’s job:
- Spring: `PathlandIndexController.framework(...)`.
- Quarkus: static `META-INF/resources` + `IndexResource.frameworkFile(...)`.
- Media assets referenced by views are absolute (`/_pathland/assets/...`) and are served by the demo hosts; server-core does not rewrite them.

Proxy sessions also construct origin URLs using the reserved base: `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/proxy/ProxySession.java` line 503 appends `/_pathland/ws?wid=...`.

4: //
5: // The served filename carries a sha-256 content hash (`dom-renderer-<hash>.js`)
6: // so a new bundle always changes the URL — the scripts are served with
7: // `immutable` cache headers, and a fresh name is the only thing that busts the
8: // cache. A tiny pointer manifest `dom-renderer.current` is written next to the
9: // copies so the SSR layer emits the right <script src> without re-hashing:
10: //
11: //   dom-renderer-<sha256-12>.js
12: //   sha384-<base64>
13: //
14: // The second line is the Subresource Integrity digest for the script tag. Stale
15: // `dom-renderer-*.js` (and the pre-hash fixed `dom-renderer.js`) are pruned so
16: // the dirs never accumulate.

20: import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

25: const hash = createHash("sha256").update(bundle).digest("hex").slice(0, 12);
26: const integrity = "sha384-" + createHash("sha384").update(bundle).digest("base64");
27: const name = `dom-renderer-${hash}.js`;
28: const manifest = "dom-renderer.current";

30: const targets = [

33: ];

I've traced the whole asset path. Here's what I found and the plan I propose.

## Current state

- `lib/typescript` builds `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js`; `scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs` hashes it (`dom-renderer-<sha256-12>.js`), writes `dom-renderer.current` (name + SRI), and copies bundle + manifest + `sw.js` **only into the two demos** (`copy-to-demos.mjs:30-33`).
- Spring starter serves `classpath:static/_pathland/**` via `PathlandIndexController.framework` (`PathlandIndexController.java:174,281-285`) but its own jar contains no bundle.
- Quarkus serves global `/_pathland/**` from `META-INF/resources` via Quarkus static resources, and mounted `/{app}/_pathland/**` via `IndexResource.frameworkFile` (`IndexResource.java:114-123,213-235`). Its extension jar only ships `sw.js`.
- `PathlandAssets` (`PathlandAssets.java:41-45`) already resolves the manifest from `META-INF/resources/_pathland/`, `static/_pathland/`, or `_pathland/` on the classpath.
- Only the demos carry the committed bundle, so every consumer must copy it themselves.

I verified Quarkus's `StaticResourcesProcessor` scans `META-INF/resources` across **all runtime classpath elements** (including dependency/extension jars) and registers them for native image, so an extension-jar bundle is served automatically.

## Proposed plan

1. **Make the build copy into the libraries, not the demos**
   - Retarget `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs` (rename to `copy-to-libs.mjs`) to:
     - `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`
     - `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`
   - Copy bundle + manifest + `sw.js` to both; keep hashing/pruning. Remove the separate extension-only `sw.js` copy (now part of the loop).
   - Update `package.json` (`copy-to-libs`, `build:all`), CI drift check (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:226-229`), README/status docs.

2. **Remove the demo-owned copies**
   - Delete the bundle/manifest/sw.js from `pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources/static/_pathland/` and `pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`.
   - This proves a consumer needs nothing beyond the starter/extension (and stops two sources of truth).

3. **Spring starter**
   - No serving code change needed: `classpathFrameworkResource` will resolve the starter jar's `static/_pathland/<file>` (app-local `static/_pathland` still wins via classpath order).
   - Update the Javadoc to state the bundle ships with the starter.

4. **Quarkus extension**
   - Global bundle: Quarkus static resources serve the extension jar's `META-INF/resources/_pathland/` automatically.
   - Mounted bundle: `frameworkFile` already reads that classpath path; harden it to prefer the application's copy (TCCL) then the extension jar, mirroring `ServiceWorkerFilter`/`PathlandAssets`, so app overrides still win.
   - Add a small `@Path("/_pathland/{file}")` fallback route for the hashed JS (static handler still wins when present) to be safe under native/edge cases, without disturbing the existing CSS/icon routes.
   - `ServiceWorkerFilter` keeps working (it already falls back to the extension jar copy).

5. **Docs / status**
   - Update `AGENTS.md:121,213-214`, `lib/typescript/README.md` + `status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md`, and `SECURITY.md` to say the bundle ships in the framework jars.

6. **Tests**
   - Spring: new `DomRendererBundleTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + MockMvc) — GET `/_pathland/<hash>.js` and `/app2/_pathland/<hash>.js` → 200, JS content type, immutable cache header, non-empty body; SSR references it with `integrity`.
   - Quarkus: new `DomRendererBundleTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) — same at global and mounted bases; assert SRI in SSR.
   - Deliberately keep test resources free of a bundle so the tests prove the library default is served.

7. **Verify**
   - `cd lib/typescript && npm run build:all` then `git diff --exit-code` on the two library resource dirs.
   - `cd lib/java && mvn -pl pathland-spring-boot-starter,pathland-quarkus -am test`
   - Run both demos and confirm `/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js` returns 200 with no app-local copy.

Two choices before I implement:

## Build & test

```bash
npm ci
npm test          # vitest (happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE apply, transport
npm run build     # tsc --noEmit + esbuild -> dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js (IIFE, minified)
npm run copy-to-demos   # copy the bundle into the Java demos' static dirs
```

The per-window-id service worker has a real-browser E2E (Chromium + WebKit) — the
worker-engine differences (e.g. WebKit reporting an empty `clientId` on navigations)
are invisible to jsdom, so they are guarded here:

```bash
npx playwright install chromium webkit   # one-time
npm run test:e2e                          # boots a fixture server + the shipped sw.js
```

## The bundle

`dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` is served by the Spring Boot and Quarkus (Java + Kotlin) demos under a
content-hashed name — `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (copied into each demo's static
resources by `npm run copy-to-demos`, which also prunes stale copies and writes the
`dom-renderer.current` pointer manifest the SSR layer reads to emit the `<script src>`).
The fresh URL per build busts the immutable asset cache.

## Transport resilience

`src/transport.ts` reconnects with exponential backoff, keeps the connection
alive with a `META::PING`/`PONG` heartbeat + no-activity watchdog, and recovers
=== ts status 15-40 ===
  batch structurally before mutating the DOM (no half-applied batch, unknown
  value types rejected). Attributed-text links and image/media sources are
  URL-scheme allowlisted (`javascript:` and non-media `data:` rejected). The
  transport rejects inbound messages over 2 MiB and closes after five
  consecutive malformed batches so the reconnect path requests a clean
  `META::RESYNC`. **SRI**: `copy-to-demos` writes a `sha384-…` second manifest
  line; the server emits `integrity` on the script tag.
- **Attributed text**: decodes `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` payloads and applies them to
  the hydrated text element as styled `<span>`/`<a href>` runs (v1 attributes:
  font size/weight/color/style/design/underline/strikethrough). An explicit
  `SET_TEXT` clears the rich-text marker; plain `TEXT`/`LABEL` updates never wipe
  rich spans. Full rebuild on payload change; the optional surgical `Range`
  fast path is deferred.
- **Window metadata**: the DOM client applies `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` at runtime — `TITLE` → `document.title`, `DESCRIPTION` → meta description, `LOCALE` → `<html lang>`; empty clears to the renderer default. `LABEL` also names buttons and slider inputs; the media shell is `aria-hidden`.

- **Single source, unified**: `src/` is the one client; `npm run build` emits
  `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (IIFE, minified via esbuild), and
  `npm run copy-to-demos` copies it into the Quarkus (Java + Kotlin) and Spring Boot demos'
  static resource dirs under a **content-hashed name** (`dom-renderer-<sha256>.js`),
  pruning stale `dom-renderer-*.js` and the pre-hash literal `dom-renderer.js` (the old
  duplicated `app.js` is long since removed). A pointer manifest
  `dom-renderer.current` sits next to the copies (content-hashed name + a `sha384-…`

Thanks — locking in your choices. Here is the final implementation plan.

## Goal
Ship the DOM renderer bundle inside the published Spring Boot starter and Quarkus extension so consumers get `/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js` (and the service worker) automatically.

## 1. Retarget the build copy (single source of truth)
- Rename `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs` → `copy-to-libs.mjs`.
- Change targets to:
  - `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`
  - `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`
- Keep the existing logic: sha-256 hash, `dom-renderer-<hash>.js`, two-line `dom-renderer.current` (name + `sha384-` SRI), prune stale `dom-renderer-*.js` / `dom-renderer.js`, copy stable `sw.js`.
- Fold the current separate extension `sw.js` block (`copy-to-demos.mjs:59-69`) into the target loop.
- `lib/typescript/package.json`: `"copy-to-libs"`, `"build:all": "npm run build && npm run copy-to-libs"`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:226-229`: run `npm run copy-to-libs` and diff the two library resource dirs.

No `pom.xml` change is needed — Maven packages `src/main/resources` automatically.

## 2. Delete the demo-owned copies
- Remove `dom-renderer-*.js`, `dom-renderer.current`, `sw.js` from:
  - `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`
  - `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`
- Fix the now-stale comments in both demos' `application.properties` (Spring mentions a non-existent `DemoAssetsConfig`; Quarkus says the bundle lives in app static resources).

## 3. Framework serving
**Spring starter** — no behavior change needed:
- `classpathFrameworkResource` (`PathlandIndexController.java:281-285`) resolves `static/_pathland/<file>` from the whole classpath, so the starter jar's copy is served at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`. App-local `static/_pathland` still wins by classpath order.
- Update the Javadoc to say the starter ships the bundle.

**Quarkus extension**:
- Global `/_pathland/<bundle>`: already served by Quarkus's static handler, which scans `META-INF/resources` across **all runtime classpath elements** (verified in `StaticResourcesProcessor`), so the extension jar's copy is picked up (and included in native image).
- Mounted `/{app}/_pathland/<bundle>`: `IndexResource.frameworkFile` (`IndexResource.java:213-235`) already reads `/META-INF/resources/_pathland/<file>`; harden it to resolve TCCL-first (app override) then the extension's own loader, mirroring `ServiceWorkerFilter`/`PathlandAssets`.
- Add a small `@GET @Path("/_pathland/{file}")` fallback route for the hashed JS (static handler still takes precedence) and set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for `dom-renderer-<hash>.js`, matching the Spring side. Existing `/_pathland/{name}.css` and `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` routes remain more specific and win.
- `ServiceWorkerFilter` already prefers the app copy then the extension jar; leave it, and update the Javadoc.

**server-core** — update `PathlandAssets` Javadoc (`PathlandAssets.java:11-35`) to say the manifest now ships in the starter/extension jars; no logic change (probe order already handles both layouts).

## 4. Tests
- Spring: new `DomRendererBundleTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + MockMvc) — GET `/_pathland/<hash>.js` and `/app2/_pathland/<hash>.js`, assert 200, JS content type, immutable cache header, non-empty body; assert the SSR page references it with `integrity`.
- Quarkus: new `DomRendererBundleTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) — same at global and mounted bases (the catch-all accepts `/app2/_pathland/...` without a real mount, as `BaseCssTest` does).
- Remove the redundant test-only `sw.js` fixtures (`pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/test/resources/...`, `pathland-quarkus/src/test/resources/...`) so the real shipped worker is exercised.
- Deliberately keep test resources free of a bundle, so the tests prove the library default is served.
- Keep existing CSS/SW tests green.

## 5. Docs / status
- `AGENTS.md:121,213-214` — bundle ships in the framework jars (not "copied into both demos").
- `lib/typescript/README.md:47,61-64` and `status.md:20,32,445`.
- `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/status.md:52-53,75`.
- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/status.md:66-68,82-91`.
- `lib/java/pathland-server-core/status.md:142-146`.
- `SECURITY.md:36-37`.
- Optional/leave as-is: `spec/DSL.md`, `docs/HARDENING.md` (still accurate).

## 6. Verification
```bash
cd lib/typescript
npm ci && npm run build:all
git diff --exit-code -- \
  ../java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources \
  ../java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources

cd ../java
mvn -pl pathland-spring-boot-starter,pathland-quarkus -am test
mvn -P jvm-only test
```
Then run the Spring and Quarkus demos and confirm `/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js` returns 200 with no app-local copy present.

Done. Branched as `feat/auto-serve-dom-renderer`.

## What changed

**The DOM renderer now ships in the framework jars**
- `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs` → `copy-to-libs.mjs`, retargeted to:
  - `pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`
  - `pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`
- Copies the content-hashed bundle, `dom-renderer.current` (name + SRI), and `sw.js`; prunes stale hashes.
- Updated `package.json` (`copy-to-libs`), CI drift check, and all docs/status.

**Demos no longer carry the bundle**
- Deleted the committed bundle/manifest/`sw.js` from both demo resource dirs; they now consume the library-shipped assets. Updated the stale `application.properties` comments.

**Quarkus serving hardened**
- `IndexResource.frameworkFile` resolves TCCL-first (app override) then the extension jar, adds `immutable` caching for `dom-renderer-*`, and has a global `/_pathland/{file}` fallback route.
- Global assets continue to be served by Quarkus's static handler from the extension jar.

**Spring**: no serving change needed — `classpathFrameworkResource` now finds the starter jar's bundle. Javadocs updated.

**server-core**: `PathlandAssets` docs updated (no logic change; lookup order already handles both layouts).

**Tests added**
- `DomRendererBundleTest` in the Spring starter (global + mounted serving, immutable cache, SSR `integrity`).
- `DomRendererBundleTest` in the Quarkus extension (global + mounted serving, immutable mounted cache, SSR `integrity`).
- Removed the now-redundant test-only `sw.js` fixtures so tests exercise the shipped worker.

## Verification
- `npm run build` + `npm run copy-to-libs`: clean.
- `mvn -pl pathland-spring-boot-starter,pathland-quarkus -am test`: all green (new tests: Spring 2/2, Quarkus 3/3).
- `mvn -pl pathland-quarkus-demo -am test`: all demo tests green.
- End-to-end packaged apps:
  - Spring fat jar served `/_pathland/dom-renderer-d14b432bd728.js` (200, `immutable`, SRI in HTML) from the starter jar.
  - Quarkus packaged app served the global bundle, `/app2/_pathland/...` (mounted, immutable), and `/_pathland/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /`.

Note: the regenerated bundle (`dom-renderer-d14b432bd728.js`) is currently untracked — add it with `git add` when committing. It also picks up the post-`77eb…` source changes that were previously stale in the demos.
